risks.note: MD&A lists this as a threat: the digital advertising industry operates within an evolving regulatory and policy environment where changes to data privacy, digital governance, consumer protection and advertising standards may influence industry practices and compliance requirements. Because the entire revenue base is digital advertising delivered on consented consumer data, a tightening of consent or data-protection rules directly constrains the targeting capability the platforms are built on.
risks.risk: Regulatory and data-privacy change in digital advertising

risks.note: The Chairman states that 'Regulatory changes affecting the Real Money Gaming (RMG) segment created near-term headwinds' in FY 25-26. This is the concrete, already-realised version of the regulatory risk: a rule change in one advertiser vertical withdraws spend immediately, and the Company has no contractual protection against it.
risks.risk: Sector-specific regulation can remove demand at short notice — the Real Money Gaming precedent

risks.note: The Chairman describes the broader ecosystem evolving through tighter privacy regulations and the gradual deprecation of third-party cookies. Loss of deterministic user-level signals erodes the identity and retargeting basis of platforms like SurgeX and ResurgeX, forcing continuous reinvestment in contextual, probabilistic and first-party approaches simply to hold performance constant.
risks.risk: Signal loss — third-party cookie deprecation, ATT and consent fragmentation

risks.note: MD&A flags that the adtech industry evolves rapidly, driven by advances in AI, automation, changing consumer behaviour and new media channels, and that these shifts can reshape competitive dynamics, technology standards and advertiser preferences. Technology obsolescence is also named as an external risk factor under the Risk Management Policy; the transition from AI-assisted to AI-autonomous decisioning means an incumbent stack can be leapfrogged rather than gradually eroded.
risks.risk: Rapid technological change and competitive intensity in adtech

risks.note: MD&A flags that operating across multiple markets exposes the business to changing economic conditions and foreign exchange movements. The Company argues the mix of INR and USD revenues is a natural hedge, but international revenue is being scaled deliberately (11.5% of FY 25-26 revenue, with the UK launched during the year), so this exposure grows with the strategy.

MD&A concedes that advertising budgets 'are still closely tied to business confidence and consumption', against an IMF backdrop of global growth slowing to 3.1% in 2026 with risks tilted to the downside — a longer or wider Middle East conflict, geopolitical fragmentation, renewed trade frictions and any reassessment of expectations around AI-led productivity. A single-segment advertising business has no counter-cyclical revenue line.
risks.risk: Demand is tied to advertiser budgets, which are cyclical and confidence-linked

risks.note: For the year under review the Company operated in a single reportable business segment; direct clients accounted for 73.9% of revenue and growth was led by Quick Commerce, BFSI, Fintech and Retail, with the business still anchored in India (international only 11.5%). Revenue quality is high, but the exposure is undiversified by segment, by client type and by geography, so a downturn in a few large advertiser categories transmits straight to the top line.
risks.risk: Concentration: one reportable segment, a direct-client-heavy book and a small set of growth verticals

risks.note: The Chairman notes advertisers expect transparency and brand-safe environments while consumers expect data to be handled responsibly, and that the Company is 'consistently fortifying our proprietary technology with AI-driven fraud detection, intelligent brand safety mechanisms and rigorous inventory quality controls'. The Risk Management Policy separately names third-party and reputational risk categories — a fraud or brand-safety failure on bought inventory is both a client-loss and a reputational event.
risks.risk: Trust, brand safety and ad fraud in the inventory supply chain

sk.overview: Broadcasting and streaming is a segment of the global media & entertainment (M&E) industry undergoing a structural shift to a 'new video economy' - the transition from traditional cable/DTH to internet-delivered video (OTT, FAST, CTV). The shift is characterised by fragmentation of viewership, globalisation of content, and a move to ad-supported models, and it is driving M&E companies to adopt cloud-native, purpose-built streaming-video software for production, preparation, distribution and monetization.
